text:
Timo Meier is one of the league's more frustrating cases in the best way: everything except the scoreboard says he's playing well. He has 77 shots in 20 games, his chances add up to 7.3 expected goals, and he has scored three. That 3.9% shooting rate is less than half of what our numbers expect from him, and the Devils have also scored 5.6 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice.

His two goals in the 4-0 win over Toronto on November 8 are the only ones in his last ten games. New Jersey has kept winning anyway, which takes some heat off.

NHL Edge puts his shot in the 90th percentile for speed and his bursts over 20 mph in the 94th. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 87th percentile for chances from in front of the net last season. A player who shoots this much from those spots does not stay at 3.9% for long. We'd watch his shot count, not his goal count.
headline: Meier is shooting, the puck is not going in
